gettingstarted.title: Getting started with the map
gettingstarted.markdownText:
## Getting started with the map

If you're new to the map or using spatial data, our Getting Started video quickly covers the basic functionality you'll need to use to add and interrogate data sets.

If you don't have time to watch the video, we suggest exploring the following areas:

1. Search for a location to quickly find an area of interest
2. Use 'Explore map data' to view the catalogue of available data sets and add them to the map
3. Interact with the data layer, including opacity and toggling on and off on the left in your workbench
4. Click on the data on the map to view more detailed data, including the raw data
5. Change your basemap using options in 'Map Settings' to help make some data sets more visible
6. Zoom and change your view, including tilting the view angle using the controls on the right-hand side of the screen

stepbystepguide.title: Step by step guide
stepbystepguide.markdownText:
## Step by step guide

Launch a step by step guide for various popular workflows below:

step1.markdownDescription: The search is at the top of the workbench on the left.
step1.title: Search for a location to find an area of interest

step2.markdownDescription: You can view the catalogue at any time
step2.title: Use "Explore map data" to view data catalogue

step3.title: Search for data or browse catalogue

step4.title: Add data to map by clicking on + sign or "Add to map" button in preview window

step5.title: Interact with data, including opacity and toggling on & off on the left in your workbench

step6.title: Click on data on the map to view more details by triggering Feature Information panel

step7.title: Change your basemap using options in "Map Settings" to improve contrast

step8.title: Zoom and change view using the controls on the right-hand side of the screen

satelliteimagery.title: Adding satellite imagery
satelliteimagery.footnote: Important: Satellite imagery can take a little while to load so please be patient. If images don’t seem to be loading, zoom out a little bit

step1.title: Find the location to view satellite imagery
step1.markdownDescription: - Use the location search or zoom and pan around the map using your mouse or the zoom controls

step2.title: Add the satellite imagery to the map
step2.markdownDescription:
- Open the data catalogue using "Explore map data" button
- Navigate through datasets to select your satellite option: Landsat or Sentinel, and daily or composite images. This can depend on resolution of the image you need (10m or 25m) and whether you want daily, 16 day composite, or annual average images
 - Select "Add to the map" to view the satellite imagery

step3.title: Filter images to find satellite imagery
step3.markdownDescription:
- Filter images by location to quickly find satellite images for that location
 - Satellites circle the globe many times a day. You can expect satellite imagery to be available for one location every two weeks
 - If you haven't already selected your point of interest on the map, zoom in to select one. You will see the filter applied in blue in the Workbench on the left

step4.title: Select a time and date
step4.markdownDescription:
- Use the date picker to select a time and date. Cycle backwards through previous years using the back arrow
 - Choose another date if your imagery is obscured by clouds. You can quickly cycle back and forward using the arrows next to the date picker

comparetimeseries.title: View and compare different points in time
comparetimeseries.footnote: Important: Any time series data can be compared using the Split Screen Mode, not just satellite imagery

step1.title: Add a time series dataset to the map
step1.markdownDescription:
- Satellite imagery is a good example of time series data, with many satellites going back decades
- Find your location of interest and filter available imagery by this location
-See our Adding Satellite Imagery to the Map guide for more

step2.title: Select the time and date
step2.markdownDescription:
- In the workbench on the left, select the time and date which will open the date picker
- Select a year, month and date, or navigate back to other years and even centuries using the back arrow
- Available dates appear in blue

step3.title: Compare different dates at one location
step3.markdownDescription:
- From the 3 dots drop-down menu in the workbench, press 'Compare' to activate Split Screen Mode
- A duplicate copy of your dataset will appear in the workbench
- Choose the dates you want to compare on the left and right of the screen
- Drag the slider using the white button to swipe and compare the two image dates

step4.title: Close Split Screen Mode
step4.markdownDescription:
- Escape the Split Screen Mode by pressing the 'x' of Split Screen Mode title in the workbench
- Remove the duplicate copy of your dataset in the workbench using the 3 dots drop-down menu

measuretoolsguide.title: Measurement Tools guide
measuretoolsguide.markdownText:
## Measurement Tools guide

Launch a guide for various popular workflows below:

step1.markdownDescription: You can find the measurement tools in the panel on the right (on desktop) or at the bottom (on mobile devices).
step1.title: Click on the measuring tools icon, to view all available tools.

step2.markdownDescription: After opening the measurement tools, select the one best suited to your needs!
step2.title: Select the measurement tool you want to use

step3.markdownDescription:
The measurement tools are designed to measure points elevation, distance, area, and angle. After selecting a tool, click on the map to make measurements.
- The point (or elevation) tool measures the elevation of different points on the map
- The line tool measures the distance between two or more points on the map
- The polygon tool measures the area of a polygon you draw on the map
- The angle tool measures the angle between three points on the map
step3.title: After selecting a tool, click on the map to make measurements.

step4.title: Check and view the measurement tool information.
step4.markdownDescription: You will now see a panel appear with information about the measuring tool being used (such as a list of points added on the map), along with a white panel that will allow you to close the tool. With the Angle Measure Tool, however, the angle will be displayed directly on the map without opening the information panel, although the white panel will still appear.

step5.title: Interact with the data via the measure panel.
step5.markdownDescription: You can move the order of the sequence of the various points inserted by changing their path, add more paths and create multi-paths, export them in various formats.

step6.title: Click on the chart icon in measure panel to open a graph based on the sampled points and monitor the elevation.
step6.markdownDescription: You can adjust the sampling steps by modifying the number of points in the measure panel.

step7.title: You can take a screenshot of the graph by clicking the download button in the top left corner of the graph.

step8.title: From the Measure Panel you can export your measurements in various formats.
step8.markdownDescription: You can choose from various formats such as CSV, GEOJSON, or KML. And you can choose to export the single path or all paths (if you have multiple paths).

playpathguide.title: Play Path guide
playpathguide.markdownText:
## Play Path guide

Launch a guide for common Play Path workflows below:

step1.markdownDescription: The Play Path panel is available after loading a file of a path or transforming a drawn path into a catalog layer.
step1.title: Play Path panel availability

step2.markdownDescription: You can draw a path directly on the map using Measurable Tools and then click on "Transform into a temporary layer" or import path files (GPX, KML, GeoJSON). Once you perform either of these actions, the path will appear in the catalog data
step2.title: Draw a path or import a file

step3.markdownDescription: Choose the path you want to play from the list and click 'Play Path'.
step3.title: Choose the path to preview

step4.markdownDescription: Move near the start point (first or last) and start the playback in a specific direction (start-to-end or end-to-start).
step4.title: Set start point and direction

step5.markdownDescription: Adjust the playback speed using the speed slider (typical range: 0.5x to 3x).
step5.title: Adjust speed and playback options

step6.markdownDescription: Press Play to start, Pause to halt mid-route, and Stop to reset the camera to the chosen start point.
step6.title: Play, pause and stop playback

step1.title: Play/Pause button
step1.markdownDescription: Start or pause the animation. While playing, the camera can be set to follow the moving marker.

step2.title: Stop button
step2.markdownDescription: Stop playback and reset the camera to the chosen start point.

step3.title: Speed slider
step3.markdownDescription: Drag the speed slider to increase or decrease animation speed. The current speed label updates in real time.

step1.title: Position the camera near the start
step1.markdownDescription: Place the camera close to the chosen start point (either true start or end) so the animation begins framed correctly.

step2.title: Adjust zoom, pitch and bearing
step2.markdownDescription: Set zoom and pitch to suit the terrain: a more top-down view for flat areas, and a less extreme low pitch in mountainous regions.

step3.title: Smooth camera transitions
step3.markdownDescription: Transitions between camera positions are eased for a smooth playback experience. Use Stop/Reset to create abrupt cuts between segments if needed.

step1.title: Improve performance
step1.markdownDescription: If playback is choppy, try lowering speed, simplifying the path, closing other heavy layers, or splitting the route into smaller segments.

step2.title: Fix camera framing issues
step2.markdownDescription: If the camera doesn't start where expected, use the 'reset camera' control or manually pan/zoom to the correct start point before pressing Play.

step3.title: Avoid low pitch in steep terrain
step3.markdownDescription: In mountainous areas, avoid very low camera pitch angles—raise the pitch or zoom out to maintain context and prevent clipping.

helpContentTerm1.content: A collection of related information, organised as one using a common data structure, e.g. "average house prices in Sydney for 2019" or "minimum and maximum daily temperature"

helpContentTerm2.content: A sequence of data collected over different points in time, e.g. temperature sensor data or a gallery of images of the same location

helpContentTerm3.content: The panel on the left side of the screen that shows what datasets you have added to the map

helpContentTerm4.content: 3D data that also has a time-series component

helpContentTerm5.content: the inventory of all datasets available to be added to the map

helpContentTerm6.content: Different map options for the blank base map, such as Bing imagery, roads, dark or light maps

helpContentTerm7.content: The dataset you added to your workbench that allows for difference calculations

helpContentTerm8.content: The way the dataset appears in the preview window. We recommend true colour to search for cloud-free images
